chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Abi Jameela al-Muradi, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Pride (al-Kibriya) is the Divine Dress; so whoever competes with Him in it, Allah will cast him headlong into the Hellfire.

key_terms.رِدَاءُ اللَّهِ: The Dress/Garment of Allah (metaphor for divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between general pride and divine Kibriya in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith distinguishes 'al-Kibriya' (absolute, unique majesty) from 'al-Kibr' (human arrogance), establishing it as an exclusive divine attribute symbolized by God's 'mantle' (rida'). The Imam warns that those who compete with God for this unique status or claim equality with Him will be cast into Hell, a concept deeply rooted in the Shia understanding of Tawhid and the rejection of divine anthropomorphism or partnership.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Abi Jameela al-Muradi from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Pride is a divine dress (suitable only for Allah) and those who compete in this matter will be hung in Hell by Allah.”
